html:
A guest who drives off I-85 and finds the SC-110 turn-off after a long day will judge your place in the first thirty seconds: the smell at the door, the kitchen counter, the bed. That is what Airbnb cleaning in Cowpens, SC really has to protect. This checklist follows the order our team works in at a short-term rental, so you can use it yourself, hand it to a co-host or hold any cleaner to it.

Cowpens sits in Spartanburg County, about 25 miles from our base in Greer, and many hosts here run a single house or a guest cottage rather than a big portfolio. A small operation has less room for a bad review, so the process matters more than the speed.

Before you clean anything: the two-minute walkthrough

Walk every room with your phone before you touch a cloth. You are looking for three things: damage, missing items and anything the guest left. Take one photo of each problem where it sits. A chipped mug or a cigarette-burn mark is far easier to sort out with the platform when the photo shows the time you took it.

Our crews begin the same way, and it ends up as a short damage and missing-item report with photos. For hosts who live out of town, that report is often the only set of eyes on the house between stays.

The turnover checklist, in working order

Dust falls, water drips and floors get walked on. The order below keeps you from cleaning anything twice.

  1. Linens first. Strip the beds, start the wash and let the machine run while you work. Host-provided sheets go back on at the end.
  2. Air the house. Open windows or run the fans. Stale air is the first thing the next guest notices.
  3. Trash and recycling. Empty every can, then reset the bins with fresh liners.
  4. Kitchen reset. Dishes into the dishwasher, then counters, sink, stovetop, microwave and appliance fronts. Check the fridge for leftovers.
  5. Bathrooms. Toilet, shower, tub, mirror and vanity, with the floor last. Look behind the toilet and at the shower drain for hair.
  6. Dusting, high to low. Shelves, lamps, headboards and window sills before any floor work.
  7. Floors. Vacuum, then mop, working toward the door you leave through.
  8. Stage and photograph. Pillows, towels, remote controls and welcome notes go back to match your listing photos.

Spots that cost hosts reviews

Most complaints we hear about are small and repeatable. Hair in the shower corner. A greasy handle on the oven. Dust on the top of the headboard. A sticky patch under the coffee maker. Crumbs in the sofa seams. None of these take long, but each one needs to be on a written list or it gets skipped on a rushed day.

Red clay is also a real factor in this part of the Upstate. Guests who hike, hunt or work outside bring it in on boots, and it stains light grout and pale rugs if it sits. Wipe entry floors early in the turnover and check the mat by the door.

Restock check: what to count every time

A restocking pass is quick if the supplies live in one place. We count against a simple list you keep in the closet.

ItemWhat we checkWhat we report
Toilet paper and paper towelsAt least a spare roll in each bathroomLow stock
Towels and linensStains, tears, correct countDamaged or missing pieces
Coffee, soap and basicsRefilled to your standardAnything you need to buy
Kitchen itemsCups, plates and utensils in placeBroken or missing items
Remotes, keys and guidebookWhere the guest should find themAnything not returned

One more habit separates hosts who rarely get cleanliness complaints from those who do: they clean for the guest's first walk-through, not for their own. Stand at the front door and look at what a stranger sees first. Is the entry clear? Is there a smell? Does the kitchen counter look empty and wiped? Fix those three before anything else and the rest of the house gets the benefit of the doubt.

How much does Airbnb cleaning cost in Cowpens?

Perfect Services does not quote a price from a text message or a listing link. The cost depends on the property size, the number of bedrooms and bathrooms, how tight your turnover window is, whether laundry happens on site, the restocking you want and how many turnovers you run a month. A one-bedroom cottage and a four-bedroom house with a pool table are different jobs.

So we start with a free in-home estimate: a short visit to see the space, no commitment, and the price comes after. You can book it on the Cowpens estimate form, call (864) 399-5168 or text (864) 666-8520.

How long a turnover takes, and booking this week

A small rental with one bathroom is usually a few hours with a team; a larger house with several bathrooms and heavy laundry takes longer. The walkthrough at the estimate gives us the real number for your property. If you have a busy weekend coming, ask for the visit early in the week so we can fit the first turnover around your guest calendar.

If the house also needs a one-off catch-up before the first turnover, a deep cleaning first gives our crew a clean baseline, and then our vacation rental cleaning service keeps it there. Hosts in nearby towns use the same process, for example short-term rental cleaning in Pacolet, and you can compare it with our Simpsonville turnover checklist.

What our method adds

Perfect Services is a Brazilian-owned team based in Greer, and the detail-first approach is the same on a turnover as in a family home: corners, handles, door frames and the edges of the floor are done by hand. Hosts notice the difference in the guest comments, which start mentioning how clean the place felt.

When you are ready to compare options, request your free estimate and tell us how many turnovers you expect each month.
